chapter: Records, Blanton, the Chicago scene, Nat Cole and Nadine
title: First jobs in Chicago: Tiny Parham, Lee Collins and Calumet City
summary: He found work through Tiny Parham, with Lil Hardin and with Erskine Tate, Lee Collins and Sonny Thompson in Calumet City for small pay.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: And I got to Chicago, and this fellow, Tiny Parham, he was a huge man. And he played organ in the Savoy Ballroom. For the skaters, and pre-prize fights, you know, like organists play for ball games and things like that? He was the house band. He played the organ there all the time. However, he would call in for dances. So he called me and asked me, he said, "I understand you're new in the city." I said, "Yes." He says, "Would you like to have a job this weekend?" I said, "Yes." So I went to the job, expecting to work with him, and it was with Lil Hardin, not him. He was playing the part of booking agent, too, you know. He had a couple of bands working around town under his name at the same time. And the -- this little inci-

dent passed. Then I started working around Chicago with the Tony Fambrough, Danny Williams, they were all around my age, 'round 20, 19, 20. Andrade -- I can't think of his -- Vernon Andrade I think. I have it somewhere. Back of my mind. Worked with Erskine Tate, Carroll Dickerson. I worked for Lee Collins. He's a legend, from Louisiana. We worked for a place similar to 52nd Street, on that Calumet City, right on the borderline of Indiana, in Illinois.
When you say 'similar to 52nd Street,' you mean there were a lot of clubs?
Yeah. We got paid two dollars a night. We had to pay the driver fifty cents, and we got a meal. So actually, we made a dollar and a half a night, and whatever we got on the weekends.
So I worked for Lee Collins.
Who else did you work for?
A boy named Sonny Thompson, that tried to play all Lester Young's solos on the piano. He played all full chords on the piano. And I can't recall the drummer's name.
